When the reachable component has exactly `n-1` vertices (one isolated vertex left), the loop completes its `n-1` iterations without ever seeing an empty `nextVertex()`, and `buildEdges` silently emits a bogus `MAX_VALUE`-weight edge.

Two fixes: `buildEdges` should skip unreachable vertices (weight == `MAX_VALUE`), and a post-loop edge-count check should catch any gap.

**`PrimsMSTTest.java`** (new): A self-contained test runner (no framework dependency) covering:
- Correct MST on the sample graph (4 edges, total weight 16)

The existing check `if (!next.isPresent())` inside the loop only fires when *all* remaining unvisited vertices are unreachable at once. In the case where the reachable component has exactly `n-1` vertices (one vertex isolated), the loop completes its full `n-1` iterations without the check triggering, and `buildEdges` would silently emit a bogus `Edge(parent, isolatedVertex, MAX_VALUE)`.

- `buildEdges()` now skips any vertex whose `minEdgeWeight` is still `MAX_VALUE` — those were never reached
- After the loop, `mstEdges.size() != n - 1` catches any shortfall: a valid spanning tree needs exactly `n-1` edges, so a deficit means the graph was disconnected

**`prims_mst.java`** — `nextVertex()` returns `OptionalInt`: the `-1` sentinel is replaced by an `OptionalInt`, making the "no reachable vertex" case explicit at the type level. The caller pattern `next.isPresent()` / `next.getAsInt()` is clearer than checking `u == -1` after assignment.
